stack_summary.notes: Monorepo of Laravel packages (rawphp/laravel-capabilities, messaging) + Go CLI (capabilities-cli). Not a full Laravel application — no app/, routes/ at root, or package.json. Source lives under packages/*/src. Unit-test-only policy (no feature/DB tests). CI: package split workflow.

critical.title: HTTP controllers lack Illuminate Request/Response bridge

locations.snippet: Controllers map real Illuminate requests into this shape at the adapter edge.

critical.current_state: Routes are registered as CapabilityController@list (etc.) onto the Illuminate router, but actions accept only HttpRequestContext and return package HttpResponse DTOs. There is no fromRequest/toResponse adapter, no Responsable implementation, and no factory that copies Sanctum user, headers, JSON body, or credential abilities into HttpRequestContext.
critical.recommended_state: Ship an edge adapter (e.g. HttpRequestContext::fromIlluminate(Request) + HttpResponse implementing Responsable or toIlluminate()) and either invokable controllers that take Request or a thin Laravel controller that maps in/out. Ensure credential/user/authKind come from middleware-resolved auth, never client claims.
critical.rationale: Without a bridge, container resolution builds a default unauthenticated HttpRequestContext (all constructor defaults), so catalog/invoke either always 401 or never see the real actor. Returning a non-Response DTO also breaks the HTTP kernel. This is a concrete prod-break for the single HTTP/CLI API (D-009) despite extensive unit coverage of pure controllers.
critical.implementation_hint: Add packages/laravel-capabilities/src/Http/IlluminateHttpBridge.php; bind controllers that accept Request, map to HttpRequestContext (user, token abilities → credential, headers, jsonBody, authKind), call existing methods, return response()->json($http->body, $http->status)->withHeaders($http->headers). Unit-test the mapper with array fixtures (still no Feature suite).

critical.title: Messaging provider never binds services; webhook uses FakeQueue
critical.current_state: MessagingServiceProvider only merges config and optionally loads routes. It never registers MessagingBindings singletons. TelegramWebhookController defaults queue to FakeQueue (in-memory list). MessagingBindings::build always constructs FakeTelegramBotClient + FakeQueue even as the pure 'production plan' path.
critical.recommended_state: register() should bind MessagingConfig from config repository, a real LaravelQueue adapter implementing UpdateQueue, real TelegramBotClient (HTTP), durable IdentityLinker/ThreadStore, and ProcessTelegramUpdate. Webhook must not default to FakeQueue outside testing.
critical.rationale: With telegram enabled (config default env CAPABILITIES_TELEGRAM true), routes accept webhooks, verify secrets, and 'queue' updates into a process-local FakeQueue that no worker drains. Outbound bot calls would also be fakes if bindings were used as-is. This is a production-break for the messaging surface.
critical.implementation_hint: Add Support/LaravelUpdateQueue using Bus::dispatch(ProcessTelegramUpdateJob); bind in MessagingServiceProvider::register from MessagingBindings::production($app); inject Fake* only when app.env is testing or via config driver=fake.

high.title: Run go test before CLI GoReleaser release
high.current_state: After monorepo tag mirror, the package-owned release workflow checks out, sets up Go, optionally notes signing secrets, and immediately runs GoReleaser. It never runs `go test ./...`.
high.recommended_state: Add a step `go test ./...` (with race optional) before GoReleaser; fail the job if tests fail so no broken multi-arch binaries are published.
high.rationale: CLI GitHub Releases are the documented install path for end users. Releasing without unit tests undoes the monorepo’s strong unit-test policy at the only binary ship boundary.
high.implementation_hint: In release.yml after setup-go: `working-directory` root, `run: go test ./...`. Prefer `go-version-file: go.mod` for alignment with module Go 1.22.

high.title: Add MIT LICENSE files to monorepo and split packages
high.current_state: All PHP composer.json files declare `"license": "MIT"`, but no `LICENSE` / `LICENSE.md` file exists at monorepo root or under any package tree (`git ls-files` has none). After split, public package repos will also lack a LICENSE file. Go module has no SPDX file either.
high.recommended_state: Add a standard MIT LICENSE file at monorepo root and copy/symlink the same into each of `packages/laravel-capabilities`, `packages/laravel-capabilities-messaging`, and `packages/capabilities-cli` so split remotes ship a clear license grant.
high.rationale: Packagist, GitHub license detection, and many corporate OSS policies require a LICENSE file, not only a composer.json field. Missing file blocks or confuses adoption of intended public packages.
high.implementation_hint: Use the same MIT text with copyright holder `rawphp` (or org legal name) in four paths; ensure split rsync includes LICENSE. Reference it from each package README footer.

high.title: DatabaseApprovalStore generates sequential process-local IDs
high.current_state: When put() omits id, DatabaseApprovalStore assigns approval-{n} from an in-memory sequence counter. QueryTableGateway already generates cryptographically random hex IDs when id is absent at insert time, but the store always pre-assigns sequential ids first.
high.recommended_state: Use random/UUID ids for durable approvals (delegate to gateway or bin2hex(random_bytes(16)) / Str::ulid()). Keep sequential ids only in InMemoryApprovalStore for unit readability.
high.rationale: Multi-worker PHP-FPM/queue processes each restart sequence at 1 → primary-key collisions or overwrites. Predictable approval IDs also weaken URL/callback unguessability if accept routes leak.
high.implementation_hint: In DatabaseApprovalStore::put, omit id and let QueryTableGateway::resolveId mint random ids, or call random_bytes like IdempotencyKey. Add unit test for uniqueness across two store instances.

high.title: Add monorepo CI that runs package unit tests

locations.snippet: ≥95% coverage … Same bar for Go CLI packages under test when CI lands.

high.current_state: The only monorepo GitHub Actions workflow is package split/mirror. There is no workflow that runs `composer test`, `composer test:cli`, tools Python tests, PHPStan, or coverage. AGENTS.md and root README document local unit suites as the contract, but CI does not execute them.
high.recommended_state: Add a `tests.yml` (or matrix job) on PR + push to main that installs PHP deps, runs Pest for core and messaging, runs Go tests for the CLI, and fails the job on non-zero exit. Optionally run `python3 -m unittest` under `tools/tests/`.
high.rationale: Hundreds of unit tests exist in-package (222 core, 32 messaging, 41 Go) but nothing stops a green local machine or a bad push from becoming the source of truth. For a monorepo that auto-mirrors to public package remotes, missing test CI is a primary reliability gap.
high.implementation_hint: Create `.github/workflows/tests.yml` with jobs: (1) php: setup-php 8.2 + pcov, `composer install`, `composer test:core`, `composer test:messaging`; (2) go: setup-go from go.mod, `go test ./...` in packages/capabilities-cli; gate split on `needs: [php, go]` or require branch protection requiring the tests check.

high.title: Gate package split/publish on green tests

locations.snippet: Push to monorepo `main` | split-packages.yml rsyncs each packages/<name>/ tree

high.current_state: `split-packages.yml` runs on every push to `main` and every `v*` tag and force-pushes package trees (and tags) to rawphp/laravel-capabilities, messaging, and capabilities-cli with no prior test job. Broken or untested code can land on consumer-facing remotes and Packagist-bound tags immediately.
high.recommended_state: Either make split a dependent job that `needs:` a tests workflow, or use a single workflow with `test` then `split`, and require the tests status check on `main` via branch protection. Tags that fail tests must not mirror.
high.rationale: Ship model is monorepo → public package remotes on push. Without a quality gate, the split is a deploy path, not just a mirror. Severity is high because consumers install from those remotes (VCS/dev-main today).
high.implementation_hint: Refactor into `jobs: test: …` then `split: needs: [test]`; for tags, fail closed if tests fail so `--force` tag push never runs. Document in docs/versioning.md Packagist checklist.

high.title: Registry defaults to allow-all when capability has no authorize()
high.current_state: stageAuthorize uses the capability's authorize callable when present; otherwise it calls the injected Authorizer. Construction defaults to StubAuthorizer::allow(). makeRegistry / ServiceProvider never bind a production Authorizer or force per-capability authorize.
high.recommended_state: Fail closed: default StubAuthorizer::deny() (or a DenyUnlessAuthorizeCallable authorizer) for mutating capabilities without authorize; require explicit withAuthorizer / host GateAuthorizer in ContainerBindings plan; document that authorize() is mandatory for non-readOnly definitions.
high.rationale: Governance is part of every surface (AGENTS.md). A host that registers capabilities with only run() gets silent allow for any authenticated actor on HTTP/agent/MCP/job. That is fail-open relative to package security claims.
high.implementation_hint: Change default to StubAuthorizer::deny(); in CapabilityDefinitionBuilder::register, reject mutating defs without authorize; add unit test that registry from makeRegistry denies when authorize missing.

high.title: Rate limiting is process-local InMemoryRateLimiter only

locations.snippet: Pure in-memory rate limiter for unit tests (no Redis / Laravel facade).

high.current_state: Config enables rate_limits (60/min defaults) but makeRegistry only applies config numbers; the limiter concrete remains InMemoryRateLimiter. Contracts/RateLimiter.php notes production may wrap Laravel's RateLimiter, but no binding exists.
high.recommended_state: Bind a LaravelRateLimiter adapter (Cache/Redis) from config when rate_limits.enabled; keep InMemory only for unit tests. Document that multi-worker hosts must use shared store.
high.rationale: Agent turn budgets and per-capability limits are security-relevant for runaway tool loops (D-008 related). Process-local counters give a false sense of protection under FPM/queue scale-out.
high.implementation_hint: Implement Support/LaravelCacheRateLimiter using Illuminate\Cache\RateLimiter; bind in ServiceProvider from rate_limits.driver; unit-test via fake Cache store interface.

high.title: Enforce ≥95% coverage in CI (policy is unenforced)

locations.snippet: Minimum: 95% unit-test coverage on package source … Below 95% is a failed task
scripts test / test:core / test:messaging / test:cli — no coverage flags

high.current_state: AGENTS.md makes ≥95% line coverage blocking. phpunit.xml includes source dirs for coverage but has no coverage report config, composer scripts do not pass `--coverage-text` / min thresholds, no pcov/xdebug is required in require-dev, and no CI job measures coverage. Coverage is only approached via ad-hoc CoverageBoost tests.
high.recommended_state: CI runs Pest with PCOV and fails if coverage for each package `src/` is below 95%. Go uses `go test -coverprofile` with a minimum check. Document exact commands next to AGENTS.md policy.
high.rationale: Policy without automation will drift: new code can ship under 95% while still greening `composer test`. Monorepo explicitly treats coverage floor as non-negotiable.
high.implementation_hint: e.g. `pest --configuration=packages/laravel-capabilities/phpunit.xml --coverage --min=95` with php-actions/setup-php coverage: pcov; for Go: `go test ./... -coverprofile=c.out` + `go tool cover -func` threshold script.

high.title: AuthController issues placeholder tokens from client body
high.current_state: AuthController is a contract stub: token() echoes client-supplied access_token or 'issued-by-host', device() returns fixed placeholders, oauthCallback() echoes query code. These routes are registered in RouteTable when HTTP is enabled (default middleware includes auth:sanctum).
high.recommended_state: Either do not register auth routes until a real host AuthIssuer is bound, or implement host-delegated issuance behind explicit interfaces (Sanctum/Passport/OAuth device flow) and never accept client-supplied access_token. Fail closed with 501/not_configured when unbound.
high.rationale: Registering stub token endpoints on the product capability API creates a footgun: if middleware is relaxed for CLI bootstrap, clients can obtain a fake bearer string that may confuse downstream gateways. Even with Sanctum, oauth/device routes are not a safe chicken-egg design for CLI login.
high.implementation_hint: Introduce AuthTokenIssuer interface; AuthController returns not_found unless bound. Split middleware: auth flows without auth:sanctum, catalog/invoke with it. Mirror shape used by CLI internal/auth package expectations.

high.title: Messaging identity and threads are memory-only with empty migrations

locations.snippet:
/** @var array<string, array{user_id: string, tenant_id: string|null, telegram_user_id: string}> */
    private array $links = [];
Conversation thread persistence (in-memory for unit tests; swap driver in production).

high.current_state: IdentityLinker and ThreadStore hold links/codes/history in private arrays. database/migrations is published but empty. No production store implementation is registered.
high.recommended_state: Add durable drivers (DB tables for identity links, link codes, threads) behind the same interfaces; publish real migrations; bind database drivers when not testing. Keep in-memory implementations for unit tests only.
high.rationale: Multi-process webhooks lose link state between requests; link codes issued on one worker are invisible to another. Conversation continuity and identity (MSG pipeline resolve_identity) cannot work under normal Laravel deploy topology.
high.implementation_hint: Migrations for messaging_identity_links / messaging_link_codes / messaging_threads; DatabaseIdentityLinker implementing ConversationIdentity; unit-test against ArrayTableGateway pattern from core package.

quick_wins.title: Stop gitignoring monorepo composer.lock
quick_wins.current_state: Root `.gitignore` excludes `/composer.lock`. The lockfile exists locally (composer.lock present) but is not tracked. Package libraries correctly omit their own locks; the monorepo root is a `type: project` workspace used for shared Pest/PHPStan and path packages.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Commit root `composer.lock` (remove ignore line) so contributor and CI installs resolve the same illuminate/pest/phpstan graph. Keep package trees lock-free for library publish.
quick_wins.rationale: Ignoring the monorepo lock produces non-reproducible CI and 'works on my machine' drift across Illuminate 11/12 minors while developing path packages.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Delete `/composer.lock` from `.gitignore`, `composer update` once on PHP 8.2, commit lock. CI should `composer install --prefer-dist` not `update`.

quick_wins.title: Add Dependabot or Renovate for Composer and Go modules
quick_wins.current_state: No `.github/dependabot.yml` or Renovate config. PHP and Go dependency bumps are fully manual. Actions used (`actions/checkout@v4`, `setup-go@v5`, `goreleaser-action@v6`) also have no automated update path.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Enable Dependabot for composer (root + packages if published separately), gomod for capabilities-cli, and github-actions ecosystem on the monorepo (and after split, on package remotes if they diverge).
quick_wins.rationale: Public packages and a token-holding split workflow need timely Action and library updates; manual-only hygiene will lag.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Add `.github/dependabot.yml` with weekly composer, gomod (`/packages/capabilities-cli`), and github-actions entries; group minor/patch if noise is high.

quick_wins.title: Add SECURITY.md for public package vulnerability reporting

locations.snippet: Public package repos: rawphp/laravel-capabilities, messaging, capabilities-cli
Package README has no Security section / SECURITY.md link

quick_wins.current_state: No SECURITY.md (or security contact) in monorepo or any package. Packages are intended for public remotes and handle authz, approvals, Telegram secrets, CLI tokens — high-value security surface once published.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Add SECURITY.md at monorepo root and in each package tree (ships via split) with private reporting channel and supported versions (0.x policy).
quick_wins.rationale: GitHub advisory UI and security-conscious consumers expect a documented disclosure path before Packagist listing.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Standard GitHub SECURITY.md template; private email or GitHub Security Advisories for rawphp org; mirror into packages/* so split remotes inherit it.

quick_wins.title: Pin Go version in CLI release workflow to go.mod
quick_wins.current_state: Release builds with `go-version: stable` (floating latest stable toolchain) while the module declares `go 1.22`. Binary artifacts can silently change language/runtime behavior across releases without a go.mod bump.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Use `go-version-file: go.mod` (or an explicit `1.22.x`) so releases match the module’s supported toolchain.
quick_wins.rationale: Reproducible multi-arch releases and fewer 'works on CI stable, fails on older go' surprises for source builders.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: In setup-go step: `go-version-file: go.mod` and drop `go-version: stable`.

quick_wins.title: Avoid cancel-in-progress for tag split concurrency

locations.snippet:
if [[ "$SOURCE_REF_TYPE" == "tag" ]]; then
  git -C "$work" tag -f "$tag"
  git -C "$work" push origin "refs/tags/${tag}" --force

quick_wins.current_state: Concurrency groups by ref with `cancel-in-progress: true`. A rapid re-push of the same tag or overlapping workflow_dispatch can cancel an in-flight rsync + force-tag push mid-matrix, leaving package remotes partially updated across the three packages (fail-fast is false but cancel aborts jobs).
quick_wins.recommended_state: Keep cancel-in-progress for branch `main` if desired, but set `cancel-in-progress: false` for tags (or separate concurrency groups) so release mirrors complete atomically per package matrix.
quick_wins.rationale: Tag mirror is the Packagist/version boundary; partial three-way sync is worse than queued sequential runs.

quick_wins.title: Idempotency defaults to memory while approvals default database

locations.snippet:
'idempotency' => [
        'enabled' => true,
        // Package default is memory; host apps may rebind a database driver.
        'driver' => $env('CAPABILITIES_IDEMPOTENCY_DRIVER', 'memory'),

quick_wins.current_state: Published defaults: approval.store=database (needs connection + migrations) and idempotency.driver=memory. Comments acknowledge host must rebind, but mismatch means multi-worker mutating invokes re-run despite Idempotency-Key while approvals may persist.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Align production defaults: both database when package is used beyond unit tests, or both memory with loud docs/health warning when memory is active under non-local env. Surface driver status in catalog health.
quick_wins.rationale: D-005 requires durable outcomes for mutating invokes. Default memory store silently fails that guarantee in any multi-process deploy while approval durability suggests production orientation.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Default CAPABILITIES_IDEMPOTENCY_DRIVER to database when approval store is database; or BootGuard warning when APP_ENV=production and driver=memory.

quick_wins.title: ApprovalPolicy any_staff treats every non-system user as staff
quick_wins.current_state: When policy is any_staff and no staffChecker is injected, every non-SystemActor is treated as staff (tenant match still applies). custom without checker also falls through to actorIsStaff.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Default deny when staffChecker missing; require host to bind staffChecker or use is_staff/roles. Keep permissive behaviour only behind explicit testing helper.
quick_wins.rationale: Hosts selecting any_staff from config without wiring staffChecker get silent open approval within tenant — contrary to multi-tenant safe defaults celebrated elsewhere in the same class.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: return false when no checker and no is_staff; unit test any_staff without checker denies ordinary user.

quick_wins.title: Align Illuminate version constraints across packages
quick_wins.current_state: Core advertises Laravel 11–13 illuminate components; messaging and monorepo root only allow 11–12. Messaging can refuse a host that core accepts, and monorepo dev cannot exercise the core ^13 constraint.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Single documented support matrix (e.g. ^11|^12 or ^11|^12|^13) applied identically to core, messaging, and monorepo root require lines.
quick_wins.rationale: Sibling packages that always ship together must not claim divergent host support; consumers will hit confusing Composer solver failures on Laravel 13.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Either drop `|^13.0` from core until tested, or add `|^13.0` to messaging + root and note matrix in package READMEs / docs/versioning.md.

quick_wins.title: Add .gitattributes export-ignore for Composer package trees

locations.snippet: Root has .gitignore; no .gitattributes at monorepo or package roots

quick_wins.current_state: No `.gitattributes` anywhere. When packages are installed from source/dist archives, tests, coverage boosters, phpunit.xml, and possibly .github can bloat installs unless export-ignore is set on each package remote.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Per-package `.gitattributes` with `export-ignore` for `/tests`, `/phpunit.xml`, `/.github` (except when release workflow must live in repo — keep workflows, ignore test noise), `/.phpunit.cache`, etc.
quick_wins.rationale: Library packaging hygiene; reduces consumer install size and accidental reliance on test-only files. Split remotes need the file inside each package path.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Place `packages/laravel-capabilities/.gitattributes` (and messaging) with lines like `/tests export-ignore`. CLI may export-ignore `*_test.go` only if desired — often Go keeps tests in module.

quick_wins.title: Approval claimLease is check-then-act without lease condition
quick_wins.current_state: claimLease reads the row, evaluates execution_lease_until in PHP, then updateWhere only on id+status. Two concurrent accept/resume workers can both pass the lease check before either writes.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Atomic claim: single UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND status=? AND (execution_lease_until IS NULL OR execution_lease_until < ?) and require affected rows = 1. Extend TableGateway if needed for SQL-side predicates.
quick_wins.rationale: D-006 requires exactly-once execution and crash recovery. compareAndUpdate helps status races, but lease claiming remains TOCTOU under concurrency — dual run() of the same approved capability is possible.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Add TableGateway::updateWhereExpr or claimLease SQL on QueryTableGateway; unit-test with two sequential claims where second must fail while lease held (ArrayTableGateway can simulate with locking flag).

quick_wins.title: CI only splits packages; no package test/coverage gate
quick_wins.current_state: Only split-packages.yml exists under .github/workflows. Local composer scripts run Pest unit suites; phpunit.xml has no coverage threshold despite AGENTS.md ≥95% blocking policy. phpstan is require-dev without neon or CI job.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Add a unit-test workflow (composer test + go test, coverage report with fail under 95%) on PR/main, before or blocking split. Add phpstan.neon.dist and a static-analysis job. Keep unit-only (no Feature).
quick_wins.rationale: Package repos are mirrored on every main push; without CI gates, broken unit contracts can ship to public package remotes. Project policy already declares coverage as blocking — tooling does not enforce it.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Workflow: setup-php with pcov, composer test:core/messaging, pest --coverage --min=95; go test -cover ./... in capabilities-cli.

quick_wins.title: Auth HTTP routes share sanctum middleware with token issuance

locations.snippet: public const PROTECTED includes ROUTE_AUTH_TOKEN and ROUTE_AUTH_DEVICE

quick_wins.current_state: All capability routes share one middleware list from surfaces.http.middleware. Auth token/device/oauth callback routes are also listed in HttpAuthGate::PROTECTED requiring authenticated presentation.
quick_wins.recommended_state: Per-route middleware: public or guest middleware for token/device/oauth callback (with CSRF/state where needed); auth:sanctum for list/describe/invoke/approvals. Gate should not treat auth issuance as already-authenticated.
quick_wins.rationale: CLI/device OAuth cannot bootstrap if issuance endpoints require the token they issue. Homogeneous middleware is a structural block for D-009 CLI client flows.
quick_wins.implementation_hint: Extend RouteTable route defs with middleware_override; HttpRouteRegistrar merges group + per-route middleware.

medium.title: Wire PHPStan (config + CI); cover messaging package

locations.snippet: PHPStan max on package code when CI lands.

medium.current_state: phpstan/phpstan is in monorepo and core require-dev, but there is no `phpstan.neon` / `phpstan.neon.dist` anywhere outside vendor, no composer script, and no CI job. Messaging has no phpstan dep. AGENTS.md defers 'PHPStan max … when CI lands' — residual still open.
medium.recommended_state: Add package-level (or monorepo paths) phpstan.neon at max level for both PHP packages, composer scripts `analyse` / `analyse:core` / `analyse:messaging`, and a CI job. Messaging should require-dev phpstan like core.
medium.rationale: Static analysis is declared as a quality bar for package code but is inert today; install cost without enforcement.
medium.implementation_hint: phpstan.neon with paths packages/*/src, level max; baseline file if needed; `"analyse": "phpstan analyse"` in root composer.json; add to tests workflow.

medium.title: CoverageGreen boost suites risk gaming the 95% floor

locations.snippet: REQ-016: exercise remaining uncovered unit paths so package line coverage ≥95%.

medium.current_state: Four large CoverageBoost* files (~2.2k lines) exist specifically to raise line coverage. AGENTS.md forbids gaming coverage with weak asserts or shipping dead code for %.
medium.recommended_state: Fold high-value asserts into domain-named suites (pipeline, HTTP, approval); delete pure line-chasing cases; prefer mutation-resistant asserts. Keep coverage ≥95% via real scenarios from requirements-inventory.
medium.rationale: Line coverage with bulk boost files can mask untested behaviour while satisfying the numeric gate, undermining the monorepo's 'tests define the product' contract.
medium.implementation_hint: Run pest --coverage and inventory which boost cases only touch getters; migrate residual paths into existing Unit/* matrices with behavioural expects.

enhancements.title: Document messaging env vars in a package .env.example
enhancements.current_state: `.env` is correctly gitignored and `!.env.example` is allowed, but no `.env.example` exists anywhere. Telegram tokens/webhook secrets and host capability env keys are only discoverable by reading config PHP or user-guide prose.
enhancements.recommended_state: Add `packages/laravel-capabilities-messaging/.env.example` (and optionally core) listing keys with empty/placeholder values, no real secrets.
enhancements.rationale: Host integrators need a checklist of required secrets; empty examples reduce misconfiguration of webhook security. Not critical because this is a library, not a deployable app.
enhancements.implementation_hint:
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=
TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=
CAPABILITIES_MESSAGING_AGENT_PROFILE=support
# never set CAPABILITIES_SKIP_BOOT_CHECKS in production

enhancements.title: Add CONTRIBUTING.md pointing at monorepo test commands
enhancements.current_state: Strong README, docs/, and AGENTS.md exist, but there is no CONTRIBUTING.md for human contributors covering PR expectations, unit-only policy, package split implications, and required local checks.
enhancements.recommended_state: Short CONTRIBUTING.md at monorepo root (and a one-liner in package READMEs linking to monorepo CONTRIBUTING for source development).
enhancements.rationale: Open-source multi-package intent benefits from a human entrypoint that is not agent-policy prose.
enhancements.implementation_hint: Cover: fork/clone, composer install, go test, unit-only rule, no feature/DB tests, do not commit secrets, PR must keep package docs self-contained after split.

enhancements.title: Fail closed early when SPLIT_GITHUB_TOKEN is missing
enhancements.current_state: Workflow documents the secret in comments but does not assert non-empty `SPLIT_TOKEN` before clone/push. Empty secret yields opaque git auth failures mid-job after rsync work.
enhancements.recommended_state: First run step: if `SPLIT_TOKEN` empty, echo clear setup instructions and `exit 1`.
enhancements.rationale: Operator DX for monorepo setup residual; reduces time-to-diagnose misconfigured forks/mirrors.
enhancements.implementation_hint: After `set -euo pipefail`: `if [[ -z "${SPLIT_TOKEN:-}" ]]; then echo 'Set repo secret SPLIT_GITHUB_TOKEN'; exit 1; fi`

enhancements.title: Add Laravel Pint (or document deliberate absence)
enhancements.current_state: No first-party Pint config or script. laravel/pint appears only transitively in the local lock via other packages, not as a project tool. No formatter CI.
enhancements.recommended_state: Require-dev `laravel/pint`, add `pint.json` if needed, composer script `format`, and optional CI `--test` mode — or explicitly document in AGENTS.md that formatting is editor-only.
enhancements.rationale: Laravel package ecosystem norm; reduces style noise in large core package (151 PHP src files). Low severity pre-Packagist.
enhancements.implementation_hint: `composer require --dev laravel/pint` at monorepo; `"format": "pint"`, `"format:check": "pint --test"` on packages/*/src.

auditors.notes: Scope: Laravel package monorepo + Go CLI — not a full application. Skipped or N/A for package libraries: frontend a11y, frontend bundle budgets, app APM/Sentry (host concern), Docker/Forge deploy, staging schema drift. Secrets scan found no real API keys; only test tokens (e.g. packages/capabilities-cli/internal/api/api_test.go). .env correctly gitignored. Database migrations under packages/laravel-capabilities/database/migrations look well-indexed with PKs (approvals, idempotency, audit_outbox); messaging migrations dir is empty (.gitkeep only). Docs quality is strong (docs/spec.md, versioning, per-package user guides, CHANGELOGs); relative monorepo links from packages appear avoided. No git tags yet on monorepo. Commit messages in recent history are structured (REQ-*/merge/chore), not wip/fix noise. Observability/ops findings intentionally omitted as residual for consumer apps, not the package bus itself.
